resources.string: This keyboard is for a physical or Bluetooth keyboard. There is nothing to tap here.
Three steps, in order. Android splits them across two settings screens and one pop-up, so this walks you through them.
Find "US-International (physical keyboard)" in the list and switch it on. Android will warn that a keyboard can read what you type; this one commits characters and stores nothing.
Pick it from the keyboard chooser. This is the same pop-up you use to switch back to your usual keyboard later.
Set the physical layout to English (US)

This app does the accents itself and never reads the system layout, so leaving yours on US International changes nothing. Setting it to plain English (US) just stops the two from looking like they disagree.
Do step 1 first: the chooser only lists keyboards that are switched on.
This device has no physical keyboard screen. Opening keyboard settings instead.
This device does not have that settings screen.
Once it is chosen, typing works everywhere: \' then a gives á, ~ then n gives ñ, AltGr+e gives é. You can close this screen.
